communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: North Truro Records
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

All documents, forms, communications (written or digital), and any other type of record(s) related to the scheduling and actual maintenance outage of the North Truro, Massachusetts radar site on September 11, 2001. The radar site is designated as a Joint Surveillance System facility J-53 with the FAA and the Air Force. 

According to FAA Form 7230-4 on 9/11/2001, the Daily Record of Facility Operation by Chief Heather Hemdal indicates that at 1200 UTC, the North Truro, MA radar was released for maintenance.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Charles Kallas

title: Enforcement and Complaint Records Concerning Hotels

communications.subject: New York Freedom of Information Law Request: Enforcement and Complaint Records Concerning Hotels
communications.communication:
Dear Records Access Officer:

Under the New York Freedom of Information Law (Public Officers Law, Article 6), I request copies of the records described below. Unless a different period is stated, the period for each item is January 1, 2021 through the date this request is processed. Schedule A, below, lists the hotel addresses referred to in several items. Where an item refers to "a hotel," it means any hotel in Manhattan, including but not limited to those on Schedule A.

For any item that the Commission maintains in a database, case management system, or spreadsheet, an export of the responsive records from that system, with the fields identified in the item, satisfies the request. I am not asking for individual paper summonses or complaint forms where a system export exists. I have obtained 311 complaint data from NYC Open Data and am not requesting the 311 records themselves, except as stated in item 1.

Publicly available 311 data shows clusters of complaints in the category "Driver Complaint - Non Passenger" at the 58th Street entrance of the Four Seasons Hotel (32 East 58th Street, including eleven complaints filed on October 30, 2025), at 7 West 60th Street adjacent to the Mandarin Oriental, at the Park Lane Hotel (36 Central Park South), and at The New Yorker (481 Eighth Avenue), with dispositions indicating that the Commission issued notices, obtained guilty pleas, and scheduled OATH hearings. Several items below are intended to capture the complaint narratives, complainant types, summonses, and dispositions associated with those clusters. I have also received information that Commission enforcement personnel were present at the Four Seasons Hotel during the summer of 2026.

Records requested

1. Complaints received directly by the Commission, other than through 311, that reference a hotel, hotel doorman, hotel concierge, hotel bell staff, or a payment, tip, kickback, "vig," or commission paid by a driver, base, or for-hire vehicle company to hotel staff in connection with passenger referrals, airport trips, or vehicle dispatch, including complaints from passengers, drivers, and licensed bases. Fields: date received, complaint source or type, location, category, disposition. This item also includes, for any complaint whose incident location is a Schedule A address, whether received directly or referred from 311, the complaint narrative or description as recorded by the Commission and the complainant type (passenger, driver, base, hotel employee, or other) where recorded. 

2. Summonses and notices of violation issued for any incident located at a Schedule A address or within one block of it. Fields: date, incident location, rule or section cited, licensee type (driver, vehicle, or base), disposition. If the Commission's system does not support a proximity search, an export limited to incidents at the Schedule A addresses satisfies this item.

3. Decisions of the Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings, or of the Commission, resolving any summons or notice of violation responsive to item 2.

4. Records of any enforcement operation, detail, sweep, or undercover program conducted at or directed at a hotel from January 1, 2023 through the date this request is processed, including June through September 2026: operation plans, deployment orders, and after-action or results summaries, whether or not summonses were issued.

5. Records maintained by the Enforcement Bureau, including the Uniformed Services Bureau, reflecting the assignment or deployment of enforcement personnel at or to a hotel from January 1, 2024 through the date this request is processed, including tour or post assignment sheets, daily deployment plans, detail orders, and overtime authorizations that reference a hotel.

6. Any list, map, bulletin, briefing, or analysis maintained by the Enforcement Bureau or any intelligence, analytics, or planning unit that identifies hotels, hotel curbs, or "hot spots" for illegal solicitation, unlicensed pickups, or hustling in Manhattan, from January 1, 2024 through the date this request is processed.

7. Records showing the location of enforcement stops, summonses, or patrol posts at a Schedule A address from January 1, 2023 through the date this request is processed, including stop logs, summons geolocation data, and patrol or post lists.

8. Records of complaints or tips referred to the Enforcement Bureau for follow-up that reference a hotel, and the disposition of each referral.

9. Records showing whether any Schedule A address has been designated in the Commission's systems as an enforcement priority location, hot spot, or similar designation, and the date of each designation.

10. The Commission's 2026 driver survey described in the Commissioner's July 2026 letter to licensees: the survey instrument, the tabulated results, and any free-text responses that mention hotels, doormen, concierges, or solicitation or hustling at locations other than airports.

communications.subject: FOIL Request Acknowledgement
communications.communication:
This email constitutes an official acknowledgement of your request pursuant to Article 6 §89(3)(a) of the New York State Public Officers Law (POL). You may keep this email as confirmation that you have successfully submitted your request for records to the New York City Taxi and Limousine Commission (TLC).

The TLC is currently reviewing your request in accordance with the FOIL statute and you will either be notified of the availability of such records or receive such records in approximately thirty business days. If your request requires more than thirty business days for fulfillment, you will be contacted with an updated estimated timeframe.
